title: Qualitative Research Methods: Case Study, Ethnography, Historical, Phenomenology, Focus Group, Action Research, Grounded Theory
summary: Case study; ethnography; historical method; phenomenology; focus group; action research; grounded theory; key steps and coding.
objectives: Match each method with its primary focus.
revision: Seven qualitative methods: case study, ethnography, historical, phenomenology, focus group, action research, grounded theory. Grounded theory = theory from data via coding.
confusions: Believing grounded theory tests existing theory.

notes.t: A qualitative research method involving an in-depth and detailed examination of a single individual, group, event, or unit.
A qualitative research method primarily used to study and understand cultural practices, behaviors and beliefs within specific communities through immersive fieldwork.
A qualitative approach that studies past events, records and documents to understand present phenomena.
A qualitative approach focused on understanding lived experiences and how individuals make meaning of phenomena.
A group discussion guided by a moderator to explore attitudes, beliefs and experiences.
Research conducted by practitioners in their own setting to solve practical problems and improve practice.
A qualitative method for generating theory from data through systematic coding and constant comparison.

i: Open coding — breaking data into discrete parts.
Selective coding — identifying the core category.

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks to match qualitative methods with their defining features. Grounded theory = theory from data; ethnography = culture; phenomenology = lived experience.

mnemonics.title: CEHPAFAG
mnemonics.text: C — Case study, E — Ethnography, H — Historical, P — Phenomenology, F — Focus group, A — Action research, G — Grounded theory

flashcards.a: Cultural practices, behaviors and beliefs through fieldwork.
